newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz takes over as anti-Islamist PM.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz takes over as anti-Islamist PM.

text.p: Conservative Mesut Yilmaz took over as the prime minister of officially secular Turkey on Monday in an attempt to deny power to the Islamists after months of political chaos.
He said his left-right coalition would put an end to tensions over the role of Islam in public life and possible intervention by the restive military.
"It will be a government that raises the profile of civilian, democratic and freedom-loving values," Yilmaz told a news conference after his appointment by President Suleyman Demirel.
Yilmaz, 50, replaces Necmettin Erbakan, who resigned two weeks ago under pressure from the army after a stormy year as modern Turkey's first Islamist leader.
The new government, a minority administration supported by a leftist party, faces a confidence vote in parliament in around 10 days' time.

Yilmaz has been boosted by a wave of defections from a conservative faction allied to Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party and now has around 12 more MPs on paper than his opponents in the 550-member national assembly.
The new prime minister said he would debate a date for possible early elections with his three government allies, in an apparent backtrack from a previous commitment to snap polls.
"Negotiations on an election date will be carried out among the coalition partners," Yilmaz said.
Yilmaz said no date for elections was mentioned in the government protocol. He said earlier this month that any government of his would hold polls in early 1998, some two years before they are due.
Many of Turkey's secularists fear that the Islamists would return to power even stronger if elections were held soon, although there are few reliable opinion polls.
Welfare came to power after narrowly winning general elections in 1995 with 21 percent of the vote.
Stocks in Istanbul ended the morning session more than four percent higher on hopes that free-marketeer Yilmaz would establish a solid government.

Yilmaz named former prime minister Bulent Ecevit as one of his two deputy prime ministers. Ecevit is a staunch secularist best known abroad as the man who ordered Turkish troops to invade Cyprus in 1974 following a Greek Cypriot coup.
Former journalist Ismail Cem, a member of Ecevit's Democratic Left Party, was named as foreign minister.
Cem takes over from Tansu Ciller, a pro-Western economist who lost much of her support by going into coalition with the Islamists last year after Erbakan levelled corruption charges against her.
Yilmaz, a staid conservative, has twice been prime minister for brief spells since 1991.
